title: Positional integer expansions and hereditary representations
proposed_reference_coverage: **Positional integer expansions: digits, finite sums, and hereditary representations**
fact_or_context_to_reference: Finite base-b digit expansions are unique and obtained by quotient and remainder. In a sum of distinct powers of two, the largest differing exponent dominates all smaller exponents; a leading length marker separates binary words of different lengths. Recursively expanding the exponents gives canonical finite hereditary representations, and replacing the base throughout the expression defines base substitution.
